decisions.reason: As a publicly presented reworking of the already accepted BASIC 518, it carries prior investment, visible commitment, and signs of market acceptance, so management would be very reluctant to withdraw it so soon.

The dedicated product page signals a clear public commitment, and as a mobile shredder it fits the firm's core waste-processing portfolio, making an early exit unlikely despite limited market evidence.

Although it was only mentioned rather than strongly promoted, the mobile high-speed grinder matches the firm's strategic direction and any weak first-year response could easily be interpreted as temporary market ramp-up.

A stationary electric fine shredder aligns well with the firm's stated push toward technical development and resource-saving recycling solutions, so sunk development costs and strategic fit favor continuation.

Even if this green-waste-specific grinder may be somewhat niche, it remains close to the firm's established applications and management would likely give it more time before admitting a failed launch.
Its own webpage indicates strong public commitment, and stationary pre-shredders are central enough to the firm's processing systems business that management would tend to persist with the product.
